title: Scroll Back
blurb: Phones, games, space and sports since 2000, scrambled up with stuff way older.

cards.say: [Tetris was invented in Moscow, back in the Soviet Union], [the PlayStation started out as a Sony project with Nintendo], [the NES first went on sale in America bundled with a toy robot], and [the first version of Minecraft came out before Roblox launched].
cards.real: Roblox launched in 2006. Minecraft's first public test version didn't come out until 2009.

cards.say: [the first item sold on eBay was a broken laser pointer], [the sideways smiley face was first typed by a professor at MIT], [one of the first webcams was set up just to watch a coffee pot], and [Google's name comes from googol, a 1 followed by 100 zeros].
cards.real: The first sideways smiley was typed in 1982 by Scott Fahlman of Carnegie Mellon University, on an online message board.

cards.say: [in 2018, a rocket launched a sports car into orbit around the Sun], [in 2023, a NASA capsule landed in Utah carrying dust from an asteroid], [in 2019, the Hubble telescope took the first photo of a black hole], and [in 2021, a helicopter made the first powered flight on another planet].
cards.real: The first black hole photo came from the Event Horizon Telescope, a team of radio telescopes linked up around the world, not from Hubble.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) NASA's OSIRIS-REx sample capsule landed in Utah on September 24, 2023, carrying rocks and dust from the asteroid Bennu

cards.say: [the very first iPhone came with the App Store built in], [the power button symbol is a 1 and a 0 mashed together], [Bluetooth is named after a Viking king], and [the word emoji comes from Japanese, not from the word emotion].
cards.real: The first iPhone came out in 2007 with no App Store. The App Store opened a year later, in July 2008.

cards.say: [in 2010, a Wimbledon match lasted more than 11 hours over three days], [at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, two 13-year-olds won gold and silver in skateboarding], [in 2014, Germany beat host Brazil 7 to 1 in the World Cup final], and [in 2019, the Raptors became the first team outside the US to win an NBA title].
cards.real: Germany's 7 to 1 win over host Brazil came in the semifinal. In the final, Germany beat Argentina 1 to 0.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) John Isner beat Nicolas Mahut at Wimbledon on June 22-24, 2010, after 11 hours 5 minutes of play
NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Germany beat Brazil 7-1 in the 2014 World Cup semifinal; the final was Germany 1-0 Argentina
NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) the Toronto Raptors won the 2019 NBA Finals, the first title for a team based outside the US

cards.say: [SpongeBob's creator used to teach marine biology at an ocean institute], [the first Harry Potter book's first hardcover run was just 500 copies], [Gangnam Style was the first YouTube video to reach a billion views], and [Frozen was the first animated movie to earn a billion dollars].
cards.real: Toy Story 3 was the first animated movie to pass a billion dollars, in 2010. Frozen got there in 2014.

cards.say: [in 2015, scientists first detected ripples in space called gravitational waves], [in 2006, Pluto was demoted because astronomers found it had no moons], [in 2013, the Curiosity rover played Happy Birthday to itself on Mars], and [in 2014, India reached Mars with a probe that cost less than the movie Gravity].
cards.real: Pluto has five known moons. It lost planet status because it hasn't cleared other objects out of its orbit, a rule for full planets.

cards.say: [Facebook was first open only to students at Stanford], [Instagram was an iPhone-only app when it launched], [TikTok merged with the lip-sync app Musical.ly in 2018], and [the first dot-com domain name was registered in 1985].
cards.real: Facebook launched in 2004 just for Harvard students. It opened to other colleges next, and later to everyone.

cards.say: [in 2001, the first space tourist flew up on NASA's space shuttle], [the Hubble telescope launched in 1990 with a mirror that was the wrong shape], [John Glenn went back to space at age 77], and [in 2015, astronauts ate lettuce they grew on the space station].
cards.real: The first space tourist, Dennis Tito, rode a Russian Soyuz rocket to the space station in 2001, paying about 20 million dollars.

cards.say: [Nintendo's Wii was code-named Revolution before it came out], [Minecraft's very first test version was called Cave Game], [Pac-Man was called Munch Man when it came out in Japan], and [the first Pokémon games were called Red and Green, not Red and Blue].
cards.real: Pac-Man's original Japanese name was Puck Man. It became Pac-Man when it came to America later in 1980.

cards.say: [in 1994, IBM sold a touchscreen phone that could send email and faxes], [in 2001, the first iPod promised 1,000 songs in your pocket], [in 2010, Disney became the first studio with two billion-dollar movies in one year], and [in 1974, the first barcode scanned at a store checkout was on a cereal box].
cards.real: The first barcode scanned at a checkout, in Troy, Ohio, in 1974, was on a 10-pack of Juicy Fruit gum that cost 67 cents.

cards.say: [in 1997, a computer called Deep Blue beat chess champion Garry Kasparov], [in 2019, a NASA lander made the first landing on the far side of the Moon], [in 2014, a space probe landed on a comet for the first time], and [Wordle was made by a software engineer as a gift for his partner].
cards.real: The first soft landing on the Moon's far side was China's Chang'e 4, in January 2019. It even dropped off a little rover to explore.
